newsitem.title: UK: UK gives go ahead for N.Sea 25,000 bpd oilfield.
newsitem.headline: UK gives go ahead for N.Sea 25,000 bpd oilfield.

text.p: The U.K. government has given a consortium the go ahead to develop a North Sea oilfield which has reserves of around 30 million barrels.
The first oil from the West Brae field is planned for late 1997 and expectations are for the field to be producing 25,000 barrels per day in 1998.

The companies involved are Marathon Oil U.K., a subsidiary of USX-Marathon Group, with a 38 percent interest, Britoil Plc, a unit BP Exploration, with 20 percent, Talisman Energy Ltd 14 percent, Kerr-McGee Oil eight percent, British Gas Exploration and Production Ltd 7.7 percent, LL&E (U.K) Inc, a subsidiary of Louisiana Land and Exploration Co, 6.3 percent, Sands Oil & Gas Ltd four percent and British Borneo Oil & Gas Ltd two percent.
The West Brae field will be a subsea development tied back to Marathon's Brae "A" platform 8.7 km away.
